blocks.text: «The number “**ОДИН**” acts as an adjective. It agrees with the nouns to which it refers in gender, number and case.

**ОДИН** (**ОДНА**, **ОДНО**) declines like **ЭТОТ** (**ЭТА**, **ЭТО**).» «Note that with masculine inanimate nouns the Accusative of “**ОДИН**” is the same as the Nominative. With animate nouns it is the same as the Genitive… The feminine Accusative is always “**ОДНУ**”.»
DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 70, p. 24. · Every form on this page is the OpenCorpora dictionary's own (CC BY-SA 4.0), put together by the rules quoted above.

Real sentences: from the library's public-domain books (author and title above each), and from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), shown with their translation. The numeral is blanked; type it in the form the sentence needs. ё and е are both accepted.

whys.one: «The number “ОДИН” acts as an adjective. It agrees with the nouns to which it refers in gender, number and case. ОДИН (ОДНА, ОДНО) declines like ЭТОТ (ЭТА, ЭТО).» «Note that with masculine inanimate nouns the Accusative of “ОДИН” is the same as the Nominative. With animate nouns it is the same as the Genitive… The feminine Accusative is always “ОДНУ”.» — DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 70, p. 24.
